name: Sorbitan Esters
aliases: E491, E492, E493, E494, E495, sorbitan monostearate, sorbitan tristearate, sorbitan monolaurate, sorbitan monooleate, sorbitan monopalmitate, sorbitan esters
what_is: A family of emulsifiers made by combining sorbitan with different fatty acids, identified as E491–E495.
why_botia: Sorbitan esters keep fat and water mixed and are used in baked goods, ice cream and coatings. In 2026 JECFA withdrew the permanent group ADI they had and replaced it with a temporary one of the same value, 0–25 mg/kg body weight: there are indications of genotoxicity in one of them, sorbitan monostearate, that remain unresolved. This is an open evaluation, not a conclusion.
can_1: Detect E491–E495 and the corresponding sorbitan ester names.
can_2: Explain that JECFA replaced the permanent group ADI with a temporary 0–25 mg/kg body-weight limit in 2026 because the genotoxicity question for sorbitan monostearate remains unresolved.
cannot_1: Determine how much sorbitan ester is present in a product from the ingredient list.
cannot_2: Treat unresolved genotoxicity evidence as proof that a declared amount of a sorbitan ester causes harm.

sources.label: EU Regulation 1333/2008 — authorised uses for E491–E495

title: Sorbitan Esters
description: Sorbitan esters E491–E495 are emulsifiers. In 2026 JECFA withdrew their permanent group ADI and established a temporary 0–25 mg/kg body-weight limit because genotoxicity evidence for sorbitan monostearate remains unresolved.
